title: Tile Roofs in Houston Suburbs
description: The tile you can see is often fine. The underlayment under it is what fails, and walking the roof to check makes more broken tiles.
html:
Katy, parts of Cypress, and plenty of newer suburbs are full of concrete and clay tile. From the street the roof still looks sharp twenty years on. Under the tile, the underlayment is a different age. That sheet, not the tile, is the water barrier.

The leak is under the piece that looks fine

Tiles crack, slip, and break when a boot steps wrong. The felt or synthetic sheet beneath them cracks from heat, shrinks at the nails, and opens at the hips and valleys. Rain gets under a sound-looking tile and runs until it finds a seam in the deck. The ceiling stain does not sit under the broken tile you noticed. It sits under the path the water took.

Walking a tile roof to “just look” breaks more tiles than the storm did. We keep traffic on the right courses and replace what we break. If someone quotes you a repair that starts with a casual walk across the field, ask how they plan to put the broken pieces back.

Repair a section, or take it all off

A few broken tiles and a sound underlayment is a repair: replace the tiles, re-bed the hips if they have opened, fix the flashing. Underlayment that has turned to paper across the field is a replacement. You cannot staple a forever patch under tiles you do not lift. Lifting the field means you are already most of the way to a new roof.

Matching tile is its own problem

The tile on the house may be a color nobody still makes. A repair then means salvaging tiles from a hidden slope, or accepting a patch you will see from the street. Say that out loud before the job starts. On a full replacement, we count what can be reused and what has to be ordered, including hips and ridges, which break more often than the field.

Some of these houses are better served by stone-coated steel that keeps the profile and drops the weight. Some should stay tile, with a new underlayment and the original tiles back on where they survived. Request a free inspection before you buy a pallet of tile that does not match. (281) 541-0027.
